principles: Fix only the real correctness gap: actual active worktree file overlap is currently invisible to parallel scheduling unless declared manually.
Keep Parallel Wave L0/read-only and host-neutral; overlap detection is guidance, not lifecycle or Authority evidence.
Preserve existing worktree, owner lease, and main write lock responsibilities instead of introducing a broad file-lock framework.
drivers: Operators need to see hidden same-file overlap before parallel DEV/merge decisions.
The existing sharedHotspots model is useful but incomplete when metadata was not declared.
The change must remain testable with deterministic smoke fixtures.

options.name: A: Add git-derived active worktree changed-file overlap to Parallel Wave safety model
pros: Targets the missing mechanical fact directly
Reuses existing parallel plan/status/merge queue surfaces
Keeps the feature read-only and local Non-authority
cons: Requires careful filtering of runtime/story metadata
Read-only guidance still depends on operators respecting the queue

options.name: B: Add a global source file lock for every edited path
cons: Likely to block legitimate independent work
Adds a new coordination framework beyond the observed correctness gap

options.name: C: Rely on git merge conflicts and validation only
cons: Does not solve the user-observed blind spot before merge
Semantic fix-A-break-B cases may not produce textual conflicts

chosen: A: Add git-derived active worktree changed-file overlap to Parallel Wave safety model
rationale: Choose A because it mechanically exposes the real hidden risk at the scheduling and merge-queue layer without inventing a broad lock or claiming Authority. It follows existing Lattice logic: worktrees isolate edits, owner leases protect story writes, main write lock serializes merge, and Parallel Wave should project scheduling hazards.

preMortem.scenario: Overlap detector reports Lattice metadata files and creates noisy false positives
preMortem.trigger: git status includes .lattice/story runtime or owner lease paths
preMortem.consequence: Operators lose trust and avoid useful parallel scheduling
preMortem.mitigation: Pin a material-file predicate and add smoke coverage excluding story/runtime metadata

preMortem.scenario: parallel_merge_queue says ready even when actual active worktree overlaps exist
preMortem.trigger: overlap is computed but not fed into safety/recommendation/blocker guidance
preMortem.consequence: The original same-file blind spot remains
preMortem.mitigation: Feed overlap as visible degradation and assert queue guidance lists file and peer story

preMortem.scenario: Overlap output is mistaken for Authority or DONE evidence
preMortem.trigger: JSON wording or schema adds receipt/proof-like fields
preMortem.consequence: Local scheduling guidance could be overclaimed
preMortem.mitigation: Keep authority boundary unchanged and assert productionDone=false, authorityChanged=false, receiptRefs=[]
